<thought>From the spectrum, the M+2 peak is about one‑third the intensity of the monoisotopic peak, matching the 35Cl/37Cl natural abundance (≈75.8%/24.2%). The sizable M+1 peak (~16 % of base) corresponds to the cumulative 13C contribution, indicating carbon is present. No other characteristic isotope patterns (e.g., Br’s ~1:1 M+2, S’s low‑intensity M+2) are evident. Thus the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
